title: finding(docs): the schema-rendering guide's Lazy Loading example authors a `tabs` node whose every key but `type` is undeclared — and `lazyLoad` is a real key borrowed from usePerformance, not a node member
body:
Path: P1 | 那条路第 1 步「写元数据」 | 已发布指南照抄即被拒

`content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md`'s **Lazy Loading** example teaches a `tabs` node in which **every key but `type` is undeclared**, so a reader who copies it is refused by the published `TabsSchema` and, after the strip, renders an empty tab bar.

## The fence, verbatim, seat-verified at source on objectui `origin/main` `1db82373f767c5331d7ce8d1bfb9beb4420f7cf5`

```
content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md:340-353

  ### Lazy Loading

  Large schemas are automatically optimized:

  ```json
  {
    "type": "tabs",
    "lazyLoad": true,
    "tabs": [
      { "title": "Tab 1", "body": { /* Loaded when tab is clicked */ } },
      { "title": "Tab 2", "body": { /* Loaded when tab is clicked */ } }
    ]
  }
  ```
```

Four keys, four mismatches against the published face:

| the doc writes | the published schema declares |
|:--|:--|
| `tabs` | **`items`** (`TabsSchema`) |
| `title` | **`label`** (`TabItemSchema`) |
| `body` | **`content`**, and it is REQUIRED (`TabItemSchema`, `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts:432`, no `.optional()`) |
| `lazyLoad` | not a `tabs` member at all — see §「what `lazyLoad` really is」 |

**[CARD-CLAIM, measured by the objectui#9941 dev against the BUILT schema, ⛔ not re-run by this seat]**: copied verbatim the node is refused — `invalid_type` at path `["items"]`, 「expected array, received undefined」 — and since the face strips what it does not declare, the surviving node renders an **empty tab bar**.

## ⭐ `lazyLoad` is not fiction — it is a key from a different surface, and that is the sharper fault

Seat-measured: `lazyLoad` **does** exist in this repo, on **`packages/react/src/hooks/usePerformance.ts`** (`:44` declares it, `:90` defaults it `true`, `:165` reads it). It is a member of a **performance-hook configuration object** — ⛔ not of any schema node.

⇒ the doc has taken a real key from one surface and taught it on another. That is worse than inventing one: a reader who searches the repo **finds it**, confirms it is real, and concludes their node is correct. ⭐ CONTROL, same command: `defaultValue` — a key the `tabs` renderer really does read — occurs on 3 lines of `tabs.tsx`, so the instrument distinguishes 「member of this node」 from 「string present in the repo」.

## ⚠️ And the prose above it makes a claim of its own

> Large schemas are automatically **optimized**:

That sentence presents `lazyLoad` as something the platform already does to tabs. ⛔ This card does **not** assert whether any lazy-loading of tab bodies exists — no measurement was taken of that, and the repair may well be 「delete the section」 rather than 「fix the keys」. ⭐ Whoever takes it must settle that first: a corrected example that still promises an optimization nothing performs is the same defect with better spelling.

## ⚠️ Not even valid JSON

The fence is tagged ```` ```json ```` and contains `/* Loaded when tab is clicked */` — a JavaScript comment. A reader who copies it hits a **parse error before ever reaching the schema**, which is the one mercy here and also why this may have gone unmeasured for so long.

## Class (c) — metadata a reader is taught, that the runtime refuses or silently drops

The three-class test, filled in: a `tabs` node is stored metadata, re-authored by others; this guide is what an author reads before writing one; the undeclared keys are **stripped** and the required one is **missing**, so the write is refused and — for a reader who fixes only the JSON comment — the render is empty with nothing naming the cause.

## ⭐ Why it is filed apart from objectui#9941

objectui#9941 is the **shipped `defaultProps` seed** in `packages/components` — what a canvas hands an author. This is the **prose guide** in `content/docs` — what a human reads. Different package, different artefact class, different reader, and objectui#9941's repair (three items respelled to `content`) touches nothing here. ⭐ Related evidence, seat-measured: `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-layout-tabs/basic-tabs.json` already spells `items[].content` correctly — so the catalog, the schema and (now) the seed agree, and this guide is the lone dissenter.

⚠️ Note on a control this seat got wrong and re-took: a first pass grepped `"items"` **with quotes** in this file and returned nothing, which would have supported 「the declared key never appears in this guide」. That reading is ⛔ VOID — an unquoted `items` hits **3** lines. The quoting was the artefact, ⛔ not an absence. What stands is only what the fence itself shows.

## Dedupe words

`schema-rendering lazy loading tabs example` · `tabs key not items` · `doc example fails TabsSchema` · `tab title body undeclared` · `lazyLoad undeclared on tabs`
